messages.text: Kalpana shows guts to go with her class in Yorkshire Oaks

metadata.summary: King George heroine Kalpana just held on to land the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks at York after a mighty scare from Sparan Nua.
metadata.content: Kalpana wins Yorkshire Oaks as gutsy display enough to see off Sparan Nua on day two of Ebor meeting | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Kalpana wins Yorkshire Oaks as gutsy display enough to see off Sparan Nua on day two of Ebor meeting Kalpana backed up her King George success with another gutsy display to see off the fast-finishing Sparan Nua in a thrilling end to the Thursday feature on the Knavesmire. Thursday 20 August 2026 16:23, UK Image: Kalpana ridden by Colin Keane (left) passes Sparan Nua ridden by Rossa Ryan on the way to winning the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks King George heroine Kalpana just held on to land the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks at York after a mighty scare from Sparan Nua. Aidan O'Brien's outsider Sugar Island was immediately sent to the front and Ronan Whelan quickly distanced himself from the field, extending the advantage to 20 lengths turning for home. But as the main players began to eat into that lead, Colin Keane sent Kalpana to give chase over three furlongs out, hitting top gear two furlongs from home, only for Jim Bolger's Sparan Nua - who got a little squeezed at one stage - to make up plenty of ground and close the gap. The line just came in time for the 10-11 favourite to hold on by a short head, giving Keane, Andrew Balding and owners Juddmonte a second Group One in the space of 24 hours, after Item had landed the showpiece Juddmonte International on Wednesday. metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton has urged his Ferrari team to "apply the pressure" to title rival Kimi Antonelli as he seeks to chase down the Mercedes driver in the championship battle.

Lewis Hamilton has urged his Ferrari team to "apply the pressure" to title rival Kimi Antonelli as he seeks to chase down the Mercedes driver in the championship battle. The 2026 Formula 1 season resumes at the Dutch Grand Prix this weekend following the sport's summer break, with Antonelli leading Hamilton by 50 points at the top of the standings. There is a huge gap in experience between the pair, with the 41-year-old Hamilton chasing a record eighth drivers' title, while Antonelli, who turns 20 two days after Sunday's race in Zandvoort, is seeking a maiden championship in just his second F1 campaign. metadata.summary: Max Verstappen said he came closer to retiring from Formula 1 than joining a rival team as he explained his reasons for extending his Red Bull contract.
metadata.content: Max Verstappen: Red Bull driver says he was 'closer to retiring' than switching F1 teams before contract extended | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Max Verstappen: Red Bull driver says he was 'closer to retiring' than switching F1 teams before contract extended Max Verstappen, who has extended his contract to 2030, explains why he wanted to stay at Red Bull and his position on F1's rules after earlier criticism; watch Dutch Grand Prix practice live on Sky Sports F1 at 11.30am on Friday, with Sprint Qualifying following at 3.30pm Thursday 20 August 2026 17:19, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen admits that, with V8 engines' potential return in 2030, there may be another opportunity for him to reassess his future in F1 Max Verstappen said he came closer to retiring from Formula 1 than joining a rival team as he explained his reasons for extending his Red Bull contract. In a relatively surprise announcement on the eve of his home Dutch Grand Prix, the first race back after the sport's summer break, Red Bull announced that Verstappen had extended his contract with them by two further years, to 2030. The four-time world champion had been linked with Mercedes in each of the previous two years, while his management were understood to have spoken to McLaren. metadata.summary: Oliver Glasner is not necessarily known for being a disciplinarian. Meticulous, yes. A self-proclaimed workaholic. But not a coach who rains down rules. At Nottingham Forest that might have to change.

Meticulous, yes. A self-proclaimed workaholic. But not a coach who rains down rules. At Nottingham Forest that might have to change. Glasner has carved a reputation as one of Europe's most tactically astute managers. Evidence can be seen throughout his career, peaking during a standout spell at Eintracht Frankfurt. There, he masterminded a Europa League triumph against significant odds and begun to catch the eye of various Premier League suitors. In 2024, Glasner was lured to the shores of the south coast, tasked with evolving Crystal Palace's playing style, a spell so successful that Palace won three trophies during his two-year charge.
